newsitem.title: USA: Urologix adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Urologix adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Urologix Inc, which develops minimally invasive medical products to treat urological disorders, said Wednesday its board of directors has adopted a shareholder rights plan.
The plan is designed to ensure that all of the company's shareholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of any proposal to acquire the company.

"Urologix currently has no shareholder with an interest of 15 percent or more, and we are not aware of any current attempt to take control of the company," said Jack Meyer, president and chief executive officer, in a statement.
"The Plan was adopted after extensive consideration by the board and is intended to protect the interests of our shareholders in the event of abusive or unfair take-over tactics," Meyer said.

The board voted a distribution of one right for each share of common stock outstanding on January 30, 1997. Each right entitles the holder to purchase 1/100th of a share of a new series of Junior Participating Preferred Stock of Urologix at an initial exercise price of $100.
Initially, the rights will be triggered when a person or group, without the prior consent of the Urologix board, acquires 15 percent or more of the company's voting stock.
In certain instances, the rights may be redeemed by the company. If not redeemed, they would expire on January 14, 2007.
Shares of Urologix were trading unchanged at 17-1/2.
